principles: Make roadmap coverage machine-countable before claiming completion.
Keep parent governance separate from child runtime implementation.
Use existing ProofStory gates before inventing new control surfaces.
Prefer explicit future or child-story status over ambiguous partial wording.
drivers: B-5082 ProofStory gates are already available in enforce mode.
The roadmap has nine remaining milestones, which is too broad for one implementation story.
The user wants evidence that scope shrinkage cannot reappear.

options.name: A: Parent ledger first, child implementation later
pros: Keeps this story small enough to review
cons: Does not finish all M5-M12 runtime work in one story

options.name: B: Implement all M4-M12 in one large story
pros: Could produce a single final milestone claim
cons: High risk of another partial DONE claim

options.name: C: Only update prose in the roadmap
cons: Does not use B-5082 machine checks
Does not prevent future scope shrinkage

chosen: A: Parent ledger first, child implementation later
rationale: The chosen option directly addresses the user concern by making roadmap coverage auditable before splitting work into child stories, while avoiding a giant underverified implementation batch.

preMortem.scenario: The parent story is mistaken for full M4-M12 implementation.
preMortem.trigger: Final status wording says completed instead of governed or assigned.
preMortem.consequence: User again sees DONE while runtime work remains unfinished.
preMortem.mitigation: Use explicit child-story-needed and future statuses in the roadmap and ProofStory ledger.

preMortem.scenario: The ledger is oversized and gets silently reduced.
preMortem.trigger: M7, M10, or M12 are removed to make gates pass.
preMortem.consequence: DONE equivalence no longer represents the original roadmap intent.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep M4-M12 as full ledger rows and clear size only through slice_plan_set or explicit child assignment.

preMortem.scenario: B-cd3a and B-43de overlap and confuse ownership.
preMortem.trigger: Both stories claim the same proof-admissibility or control-plane work.
preMortem.consequence: Parallel hosts duplicate edits or disagree about completion.
preMortem.mitigation: B-43de references B-cd3a as narrower child-adjacent work and does not mutate B-cd3a metadata.
